verdict: Yes, but merge commit f05d48e31 (their two commits plus two of mine), not their commit 55b639503 alone. At the defaults their work is the base engine: I found no difference on the 240 local dumps in the three stored modes, on the 17 local dumps, or on 8,064,000 random models per build. Their commit must not be merged as it is for three reasons, all repaired on top with a test that failed first. (1) forcing_rounding_units accepted 64 (a value they measured, stored and drew in the campaign): my model misses its row by 1.05e-6 at an exactly feasible reduced point. The range is now 0 to 8. (2) implied_band_scale (2 and 5) widens a validity condition: on my chain model five times the band gives a postsolved point 9.5e-4 outside a bound where the band of the rule leaves the column in the model. No valid other value is left, so the option is removed. (3) The range test of the options refused the default choices next to non-default tolerances (for example a feasibility tolerance of 1e-10), so presolve() of an assertion build stopped where the base engine ran. The other 17 option values hold: 90,720,000 campaign models with the option drawing on their commit, 85,680,000 with each value pinned on the final engine, 41,555 tiny models judged in exact rational arithmetic in 40 to 44 option sets, the check tool on the 17 and the 240 local dumps; no wrong result. Their table reproduces line by line with the final binary. Not done: nothing ran with a solver, on the node (no remote command was allowed, so the two slots were not used) or on the 40 testbed instances; the full campaign size (20 and 10 million per profile option) ran on their commit, the final engine got the pinned runs and a smaller drawn campaign; one base behaviour I show with a model (the implied-bound band times the growth limit gives 1.5e-4 at the defaults) is left as it is and is the owner's decision.
commit: f05d48e3101276b7f3f18cdff5fcc753fd0d0358 (on top of a017fa221, on top of their 55b639503 and d15144a21; base fa8430e247179aed4bb23283e57f7aee648123fb)
wrong_results: REPAIRED. forcing_rounding_units = 64 (every value above 8; their range went to 90). Input: k + y <= 1e8 with k integer in (-inf, 1e9] without cost, y continuous in [0, 6e7], and y + v >= 3 with a binary v; only the forcing column active. Reduced point y = 49999999.00000105, v = 1 (exactly feasible). The row leaves k the value 50000000.99999895; with 64 units the undo takes it as 50000001 and the row is missed by 1.05e-6 (check_point: infeasible); with 90 units and y = 49999999.0000012 by 1.2e-6; with 8 units k = 50000000 and the point is feasible. The structure check was silent at 64 and 90 (it follows the band of the stack). Their header argued the range with the side alone; the band is units * rounding unit * (|side| + terms of the rest). Repair: the range is 0 to 8 (choices_in_range, tools); 64 is gone from the campaign draw, the tests and the stored runs. Test switches_review_forcing_band_above_the_rule_misses_the_row (on their commit choices_in_range accepted 64).

REPAIRED by removal. implied_band_scale = 5 (every value above 1). Input: x + 1000 y + w = 500 and y + 0.5 z + 0.5 v = 1; x continuous in [-501, 499.99905], y continuous in [9.5e-7, 1], w continuous in [0, 1] with cost 1, z and v binary with cost -1. At the default y is no free singleton column after x left (its lower bound is 9.5e-7 from what the row gives, outside the band of 2e-7), it leaves as a zero-cost singleton column and the postsolved point is feasible (row violation 9.5e-7). With --implied-band-scale 5 on their binary both x and y leave as free singleton columns, the reduced model is empty, and the postsolved point is x = 500, y = 0: bound violation 9.5e-4, structure check silent. Their header said the factor keeps the band within the feasibility tolerance; it left out that a column restored after one that passed its bound by the band passes its own by the band times their ratio (up to the growth limit of 1000). Every value above 1 does this on a model where the default does not, and a value below 1 breaks the fixed-point contract (as they say), so the option, its flag --implied-band-scale, its two campaign values and its test are removed. Test switches_review_bound_beyond_the_band_is_not_implied holds the model at the band of the rule.

REPAIRED. Broken contract at the defaults: choices_in_range(options_t()) depended on the tolerances. With options.tol.feasibility = 1e-10 (below 1e5 * tol.side_error), with tol.side_error = 1e-16 (below 8 rounding units), or with tol.activity_error_share above 0.5, the default choices were out of range, and the assertions in presolve() and in the family stopped an assertion build ('gprs_assert failed: choices_in_range(options) at presolve.cpp:562') on options that the base engine takes. The release build was not affected. Repair: the defaults are in range with every tolerance; the ranges bind the other values only. Test switches_review_defaults_take_every_tolerance (failed and aborted on their commit).

NOT REPAIRED, not from the switches: the base engine at the defaults. The same chain with y in [1.5e-7, 1] and x in [-501, 499.99985]: the lower bound of y is within the band, x and y both leave, and the only (empty, exactly feasible) reduced point postsolves to x = 500, 1.5e-4 above its bound, with the structure check silent. The base binary fa8430e24 and the final binary give the same. This is the stacking of the implied-bound band (AS-088) with the growth limit (AS-094) that the M1 validity review lists as remaining by design; it is none of the known classes (a) to (c). A repair (for example the band divided by the growth factor of the column) changes results at the defaults, so I left it for the owner.

other_defects: Their header contract of growth_ratio was incomplete: 'an integer column brings none: the postsolve rounds it' covers the integer columns of the reduced point only. It is right because every record gives an integer column an integer inside its bounds (fixed value integral; an alias between integer columns has its scale and offset rounded to integers in src/alias_forest.cpp:47-63, which I confirmed on a model with the coefficient 1.0000000005: the record is x3 = 1 * x1 + 0; defined and forcing records round). The contract now says so, and that neither form changes the band-times-ratio stacking.

Their sentence on HiGHS under dual_integer_pivots left out a condition. Checked in the HiGHS source (commit 283bfc8, highs/presolve/HPresolve.cpp, singletonCol, lines 2450-2469): the row dual bounds are updated from the singleton column only when it is not an integer column, and the substitution of an integer column needs isDualImpliedFree(row), isImpliedFree(col) and isImpliedIntegral(col). Their text said 'only on an equation or with a sign from another column'; I added 'and then only when the column is implied integral'. Their measured claim holds: with the option off the engine equals the stored m1_a on 8 of the 10 instances that change (240 local dumps).

A claim of the M1 worth report and of register entry AS-339 that does not hold: the lead over m1_a on roi5alpha10n8 does not come from integer pivot columns. That instance has no integer pivot on an inequality (counter integer_pivots_dual 0) and keeps its size (2,209,309 / 2,920 / 30,297 against m1_a 2,215,032 / 2,921 / 30,298) with dual_integer_pivots off. The integer pivots are on exactly 10 instances (academictimetablesmall, brazil3, seymour, seymour1, momentum1, savsched1, co-100, mcsched, comp07-2idx, fast0507).

Weak check: the structure check cannot see a forcing band that is too wide. On my model it is silent at 64 and at 90 units while check_point rejects the postsolved point. Their statement 'structure check and crush check pass for all 31 option settings' was true and covered two settings that give wrong results.

switches.option: options_t::dual_integer_pivots, default true, other value false; tool flag --no-dual-integer-pivots.
switches.validity: Off only refuses reductions, so the result is right for that reason alone. switches.choice: The zero-cost singleton rule and the forcing column are off in primal-only mode although both are exact projections.
switches.option: options_t::primal_projections, default false, other value true; tool flag --primal-projections; acts only with --primal-only.
switches.validity: Both are exact projections and the removed columns cost nothing, so every feasible point crushes, by dropping the columns, to a feasible point of equal objective, and dual_findings stays 0. That is what the callers of the mode rely on as far as I read them: cuOpt switches dual reductions off when a set-solution callback exists so that user assignments can be crushed (cpp/src/mip_heuristics/solve.cu:735-736, adapter cpp/src/presolve/gprs_presolve.hpp:48-49), and DESIGN.md section 8 asks that every feasible point crushes to a reduced-feasible point of equal objective. What the mode loses: postsolve(crush(x)) can differ from x in the columns of interval and forcing records and in columns restored from them. Clause 5 of the crush check exempts exactly those.

switches.choice: The growth ratio of a free singleton column reads the largest coefficient of every other free column of the pivot row and applies to integer pivot columns too.
switches.option: options_t::growth_ratio, default all_columns, other values continuous_columns and integer_pivot_exempt; tool flag --growth-ratio <all|continuous|integer-exempt>; next to pivot_growth_limit (--pivot-growth-limit) and saved_row_factor, which are unchanged.
switches.validity: The limit bounds what a restored value multiplies a deviation by, and an integer column brings none because every record gives it an integer inside its bounds: reduced integer columns are rounded before any undo, fixed values are integral, an alias between integer columns has an integral scale and offset (checked in the source and on a model), defined and forcing records round. An integer pivot column has only integer columns next to it. So both forms are as right as the default for a deviation of the reduced point. None of the three forms bounds the other stacking: a column that passes its bound by the implied-bound band takes a column restored after it past its bound by the band times their ratio (1.5e-4 on my model at the defaults); the forms do not add to it, because the ratio over the continuous columns is limited in all of them.

assumptions.title: The widest forcing band is the default
assumptions.statement: forcing_rounding_units is accepted from 0 to 8. Eight units is the constant of the base; I took it as the widest band that is right. It keeps the row within the tolerance while 8 rounding units of |side| + the terms of the rest stay below it, that is for terms up to about 1e9; with larger terms the default itself takes the value further (base behaviour, not changed).
assumptions.alternatives: A band in units of the feasibility tolerance; a band that scales with the side only
assumptions.measured: 0 units: 0 of 240 reduced models change; model at 64 units: row missed by 1.05e-6

assumptions.title: The default choices are in range with every tolerance
assumptions.statement: choices_in_range accepts side_guard_scale == 1 (compared exactly) whatever tol.side_error and tol.feasibility are; the two inequalities of the range bind only a factor other than 1.
assumptions.alternatives: Require the tolerance relations for the default as well (their form, which stopped presolve() of an assertion build on tolerances that the base engine takes)

assumptions.title: The lower end of side_guard_scale copies a private constant
assumptions.statement: The lower end of the range, side_guard_scale * tol.feasibility >= 1e5 * tol.side_error, holds the literal 1e5, which is plain_size of gpu_presolve/src/state_storage.cpp:86 (the size up to which fixed terms leave a row without an event). Nothing ties the two; the author did not list it.
assumptions.alternatives: A named constant shared by the state and the header
assumptions.measured: not measured; the guards refuse nothing on the 240 local dumps

assumptions.title: Eight rounding units count one record on a row
assumptions.statement: The upper end of side_guard_scale (11 with the default tolerances) leaves room for eight rounding units of the largest side read. A row that the zero-cost singleton columns leave in several visits collects one unit of its sides per visit at an extreme point, in every setting; the room is used up after about 90 / factor such visits. The author's range argument did not say this; the header does now.
assumptions.alternatives: No factor above 1; a count of the visits per row
assumptions.measured: 8: 0 of 240 reduced models change, 33 of 5,040,000 pinned campaign results change, no failure; no model with a ladder of visits was built

assumptions.title: Integer columns are restored exactly, which the two narrower growth forms rest on
assumptions.statement: continuous_columns and integer_pivot_exempt are right only while every record gives an integer column an integer inside its bounds: rounding of the reduced point, integral fixed values, aliases between integer columns with rounded scale and offset, rounding in defined and forcing records. A later rule that restores an integer column otherwise (an implied-integer conversion, a lock alias, a merge of columns) has to be read against this.
assumptions.alternatives: Keep the limit for integer columns (the default)
assumptions.measured: Model with the coefficient 1.0000000005 on an integer pair: the alias record has scale 1 and offset 0

assumptions.title: The continuous form of the growth ratio costs a scan on the family's budget
assumptions.statement: growth_ratio continuous_columns scans the pivot row once more for every candidate that reaches the growth test and spends those slots on the budget of the call, so a call can stop on its budget earlier than with the default form. The author did not list it.
assumptions.alternatives: Collect the largest continuous coefficient in the scan of the visit
assumptions.measured: not measured apart; no call stops on its budget on the 240 local dumps (calls_stopped 0)

assumptions.title: Where an integer column is counted with dual_integer_pivots off
assumptions.statement: With the option off an integer singleton column on an inequality counts in refused_integer before the side, cost and implied-bound tests, whatever else would refuse it, so the other refusal counters of a run with the option off are not comparable column by column with a default run.
assumptions.measured: counter refused_integer is 0 at the default on the 240 local dumps

assumptions.title: The structure check follows the forcing band of the stack
assumptions.statement: The structure check replays an integer forcing column with postsolve_t::forcing_rounding_units as the stack carries it and accepts the engine's neighbouring integer inside that band, so it cannot say that a band is too wide; only a point check (the oracle, check_point, the crush check with points) can.
assumptions.alternatives: The check tests the saved row at the engine's value with the feasibility tolerance
assumptions.measured: silent on my model at 64 and at 90 units, where check_point rejects the point
